summary: Prioritize industrial control-system risks, plan safe safeguards, and build OT security action artefacts. Explore the five-day training course.
lede: OT and ICS cybersecurity focuses on assessing control-system exposure while protecting safe, reliable operations. For OT engineers, security specialists, and operations managers, the training develops practical ways to map assets and connections, trace threats to process impact, prioritize vulnerabilities in operational context, plan network boundaries, and prepare incident response decisions. Scenario exercises produce working artefacts for coordinating prioritized safeguards across engineering, operations, and leadership.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for intermediate practitioners who work directly with industrial control systems or make operational decisions about their security. It suits technical specialists and operational leaders who need to assess OT exposure without treating safety and production continuity as afterthoughts.
modules: Purdue Model and OT Asset Mapping
MITRE ATT&CK for ICS Threat Paths
OT Security Metrics and Leadership Reporting
prerequisites: Working knowledge of industrial operations, control systems, or cybersecurity is expected. No programming is required; exercises use scenario records and planning artefacts rather than live control-system access.
